All services currently score 100, as no static analysis rules for service boundaries were violated. This score does not cover runtime-only dependencies, as the runtime call graph could not be queried for this run (`queried: false`).

No layering violations were found in any service. Folder instability metrics show healthy profiles across all services: domain layers are stable (e.g., checkout I=0.17, inventory I=0.24, notification I=0.07) and transport layers are appropriately unstable (e.g., checkout I=0.82, inventory I=0.66, notification I=0.78). The score only validates dependencies between layers, not the correctness of logic within them.

The coupling score is based on efferent (outgoing) static dependencies from one service to another. No such dependencies were found for any service, so all services score 100. This score does not reflect runtime coupling, as Cloud Trace was not queried for this run. It also does not score afferent (incoming) dependencies.

The platform duplication score is the average of service-level duplication scores. All services currently score 100. This score reflects duplication *within* a service boundary. Duplication *between* services is measured as part of cross-service-integrity and does not affect this score.

The score is reduced due to two instances of cross-service duplication between the `checkout` and `notification` services. The duplicated files are:
- `services/checkout/src/domain/ports/logger.ts` and `services/notification/src/domain/ports/logger.ts`
- `services/checkout/src/infrastructure/file-body-store.ts` and `services/notification/src/infrastructure/file-body-store.ts`
This represents a violation of cross-service boundaries.
recommendations: Consolidate the `logger.ts` port definition into a shared library or decide which service should own the canonical definition.
Abstract the `file-body-store.ts` logic into a shared infrastructure library that both services can import, removing the direct code copy.
